newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall on stronger-than-expected data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall on stronger-than-expected data.

text.p: Blue-chip stock prices fell Monday stronger-than-expected manufacturing and home sales data shook Wall Street, one day before the Federal Reserve meets to weigh monetary policy.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 27.14 points at 7,660.58 after losing more than 50 points in early morning.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 14-10 on moderate volume of 232 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 1.18 points to 1,439.33.

The two economic reports, which revived lurking fears about inflation and economic growth, compounded the market's qualms ahead of Tuesday's meeting of Federal Reserve's interest rate-setting body, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
The 30-year Treasury bond lost nearly a full point, raising its yield to 6.81 percent from 6.74 percent on Friday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Financial markets reeled after the Chicago Purchasing Manager's Index for June jumped to a 61.5 reading in June compared to 56.8 reading in May.
An index below 50 in the Chicago regional data signals a slowing manufacturing economy while a reading above 50 suggests expansion.
Single-family home sales for May rose more than anticipated, increasing by 7.1 percent to an 825,000-unit annual rate.

"People had been inclined to sit on their hands going into the FOMC meeting, but these two numbers were too strong for investors to ignore," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.
The Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday will hold the first of two days of meetings but is expected to leave interest rates unchanged.
"Now the street is concerned that tomorrow's NAPM (National Association of Purchasing Managers) index will also be strong," Orlando said.
The next key report is due Tuesday when the association releases its index of manufacturing activity.
The index was expected to show a reading of 56.4 for June vs. 57.1 in May.
"There's a sort of malaise, a pall over equities," said Doug Myers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.
Many investors were staying on the sidelines ahead of the FOMC meeting and the June employment report due Thursday, he said.
Among particular issues, J.P. Morgan & Co. lost 1-5/8 to 105-1/8 after the mutual fund company American Century Cos. said it was discussing the sale of a minority stake to J.P. Morgan.
JP Foodservice Inc. was off 1-5/8 at 28-1/2, after the company said it agreed to acquire Rykoff-Sexton Inc. in a deal worth $1.4 billion. Rykoff rose 3-5/8 to 23-1/4.
